content_of_post_to_comment: Too much Stephen King hate on here. The Shining is just a straight up banger and Pet Sematary rocks start to finish. The Dark Tower books are inventive and smart (especially 2-5) and when King wants to do literary well he does. Hmu and I’ll send a whole list of examples. If anything he was my gateway to Cormac McCarthy and Bradbury and a couple others
comment: King is interesting because genre can hide literary ambition. The question isn't whether horror is "serious" fiction, but why some writers use fear to explore grief, memory, and human weakness better than realism does.
